stops.note: contracted from older 'aevitas', from 'aevum', eternity, the root of 'eternal'
formed with the suffix -age, as in Vulgar Latin 'aetaticum'
first recorded around 1275 in the Kentish Sermons, English translations of the French sermons of Maurice de Sully; 'Stone Age' and 'Bronze Age' were coined in the 1800s

current_meaning: the length of time something has existed; a historical period
